scope: All 7 route/method pairs (GET /api/health, POST /api/login, GET/POST /api/bugs, GET/PUT/DELETE /api/bugs/:id) plus unknown /api paths and unsupported methods: 112 curl requests through the Vite proxy (http://localhost:5173/api), spot-checked direct on :3002. Input classes: valid, each missing field, number/null/array/object types, blank and whitespace-only, lower/mixed/padded/invalid severity and state, non-numeric id, missing numeric id, 1abc, decimal, hex, negative, zero, huge id, malformed JSON, body null/array, missing and text/plain Content-Type. Port-change slice: repo-wide grep of specs, README and docs for 3000.
commands: curl -s http://localhost:5173/api/bugs | node -e '<shape check: keys id,title,severity,owner,description,state; enums HIGH|MID|LOW, OPEN|CLOSED>'

findings.title: POST /api/login returns 500 HTML with a stack trace when username is a number, array or object
findings.requirement: Contract break: a client input error must produce a 4xx JSON {error,message} body like every other login failure; the bug routes already coerce non-strings to "".
findings.evidence: {"username":123}, {"username":["buggy"]} and {"username":{}} each returned 500 text/html 'TypeError: username.trim is not a function' with absolute file paths (/Users/.../backend/src/authService.ts:19:36). `as string` is a compile-time cast only; `?? ""` only catches null/undefined. Server stayed up (health 200 afterwards). Saved: evidence/contract/500-login-username-number.html, probe-results.tsv L15/L17/L21.
findings.fix: In index.ts use the same guard as the bug routes: const username = typeof req.body?.username === "string" ? req.body.username : ""; (and likewise for password).

findings.title: Malformed JSON body (and a bare `null` body) returns Express's HTML 400 page with a stack trace, not a JSON error
findings.requirement: Contract break: every /api error response is JSON {error,message}; body-parser failures bypass that shape.
findings.location: backend/src/index.ts:11 (express.json() with no error handler anywhere before app.listen at :184)
findings.evidence: POST /api/login, POST /api/bugs, PUT /api/bugs/13 with '{"title":' and DELETE with '{bad' all returned 400 text/html 'SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input' with node_modules paths. Body 'null' on POST /api/login also 400 HTML (strict mode). Saved: evidence/contract/400-malformed-json.html, probe rows L22, L26, C25, P17, D10.
findings.fix: Add a final error middleware: app.use((err, _req, res, _next) => { if (err.type === "entity.parse.failed") return res.status(400).json({ error: "invalid_json", message: "Request body must be valid JSON." }); res.status(500).json({ error: "internal_error", message: "Unexpected server error." }); });

findings.title: Bug id parsing accepts trailing garbage: /api/bugs/15abc, /13.9 and /%2013 act on the real bug, including DELETE
findings.requirement: Contract break: the route documents invalid_id (400) for a non-numeric id; parseInt("15abc",10)=15 so the check at the handler never fires. Negative and hex ids also return 404 not_found instead of 400 invalid_id.
findings.evidence: GET /api/bugs/13abc -> 200 bug 13; GET /api/bugs/13.9 -> 200 bug 13; GET /api/bugs/%2013 -> 200 bug 13; PUT /api/bugs/13abc -> 200 and wrote title '[contract] via 1abc' to bug 13; DELETE /api/bugs/15abc -> 204 and GET /api/bugs/15 then 404 (bug deleted). GET/PUT/DELETE /api/bugs/-1 -> 404 not_found; /api/bugs/0x1 -> 404 (parsed as 0). Probe rows R04, R05, R07, R09, R10, P23, P24, D06-D08.
findings.repro: ID=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:5173/api/bugs -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"title":"[contract] x","severity":"low","owner":"buggy","description":"d"}' | sed -E 's/.*"id":([0-9]+).*/\1/'); curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X DELETE http://localhost:5173/api/bugs/${ID}abc; curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://localhost:5173/api/bugs/$ID   # 204 then 404
findings.fix: Replace parseInt with a strict check in one helper: if (!/^[1-9]\d*$/.test(req.params.id)) return 400 invalid_id; const id = Number(req.params.id);

findings.title: Unknown /api/* paths and unsupported methods return Express's HTML 404 page, not JSON
findings.requirement: Contract break: api-conventions.md reserves /api for the API; responses under it should be JSON. Wrong method on a known path is 404 rather than 405.
findings.evidence:
GET /api/nope, POST /api/nope, POST /api/health, GET /api/login, PATCH /api/bugs/1, DELETE /api/bugs -> 404 text/html '
Cannot GET /api/nope
'. Same on :3002 direct. Probe rows H2, U1, U2, U4, U5, D11.
findings.fix: Before app.listen: app.use("/api", (_req, res) => res.status(404).json({ error: "not_found", message: "Route not found." }));

findings.title: Invalid severity reports error code `blank_severity`; wrong-type fields report `blank_*`
findings.requirement: Contract break: the service distinguishes INVALID_SEVERITY from BLANK_SEVERITY but the route collapses both into blank_severity, so a client cannot tell 'critical' from ''. Non-string values (title:42, owner:7, severity:["high"]) are coerced to "" and reported as blank ('Title is required.').
findings.evidence: POST severity 'critical' -> 400 {"error":"blank_severity"}; PUT severity 'urgent' -> 400 blank_severity; POST title 42 -> 400 blank_title; PUT owner 5 -> 400 blank_owner. Also PUT with state omitted -> invalid_state while severity omitted -> blank_severity (inconsistent missing-field vocabulary). Frontend keys only on `message` for bug errors, so no UI impact today. Probe rows C16, C17, C19, C20, C22, C23, P03, P13, P15, P16.
findings.fix: Split the case: case "INVALID_SEVERITY": res.status(400).json({ error: "invalid_severity", message: "Severity must be high, mid, or low." }). Optionally return invalid_type for non-string fields.

findings.title: A valid JSON body without Content-Type: application/json is silently read as empty and reported as blank fields
findings.requirement: Contract break (minor): a body the server cannot parse should be 415, not a misleading validation error.
findings.evidence: POST /api/login with a correct JSON body and no Content-Type (curl default form-urlencoded) or text/plain -> 400 missing_credentials; POST /api/bugs -> 400 blank_title; PUT -> 400 blank_title. Probe rows L23, L24, C26, P18.
findings.fix: For POST/PUT under /api, reject when !req.is("application/json") with 415 {error:"unsupported_media_type"}.

findings.title: Whitespace-only password is treated as a real password (401) rather than blank (400 blank_password)
findings.requirement: Business rule, ambiguous: 03-login.md requires a blank-password error and specifies trimming only for the username. Behaviour is confirmed; whether '   ' counts as blank is a product decision.
findings.evidence: {"username":"buggy","password":"   "} -> 401 invalid_credentials. Whitespace-only username -> 400 blank_username. Probe rows L09, L11.
findings.fix: Ask product. If blank: use password.trim() === "" for the blank checks only, still comparing the untrimmed password.

findings.title: No API contract document and no API tests exist
findings.requirement: Every endpoint's status and shape should be pinned by a documented contract and at least one test per status; today only api-conventions.md (the /api prefix) exists and the only test file targets playwright.dev.
findings.evidence: The contract in contract.md is reconstructed from index.ts. Lead's suite is 6/6 of example.spec.ts, which never calls /api. Backward compatibility cannot be judged.
findings.fix: Commit the reconstructed contract to specs/engineering/api-conventions.md and add tests/contract/*.spec.ts using Playwright `request` (one status per test), starting from probe.sh's cases.

notTested: Baseline (origin/main) was not run; findings are attributed as pre-existing because git diff shows no route, handler or service change, only PORT 3000 -> 3002 (code-reading attribution).
Authentication on the bug routes: all bug endpoints accept unauthenticated requests (observed throughout) - owned by security, not filed here.
Stack-trace disclosure in 500/400 HTML pages is noted in contract-01/02 as evidence; its security rating belongs to security.
Owner is not validated against users.json (POST owner 'nobody-at-all' -> 201); 06-create-bug.md does not state it must be a known user, so not filed.
Large payloads (>100kb body-parser limit -> 413 shape), very long strings, unicode/control characters, concurrent writes.
CORS behaviour beyond observing headers on :3002 (OPTIONS /api/bugs returns 200 text/html 'GET,HEAD,POST').
HEAD requests, query-string filtering (GET /api/bugs?state=closed ignores the query, as expected - no filter in the contract).
No Playwright spec was written; curl probe is the evidence.
